A gluten free stuffing recipe doesn’t have to be complicated, dry, or taste different With the right gluten free bread, proper moisture control, and classic herbs like sage, thyme, and rosemary, you can make a moist gluten free stuffing, a crispy gluten free stuffing, or a perfectly soft stuffing that fits right into any gluten free thanksgiving dinner or gluten free holiday side dish spread.

This guide walks you through everything from stuffing without gluten basics to oven, stovetop, and gluten free stuffing crock pot methods. Whether you’re cooking for celiac disease, wheat sensitivity, or just want a reliable homemade gluten free stuffing, this page covers it all.

What Is Gluten-Free Stuffing?

Gluten-free stuffing is a classic stuffing made using gluten free bread, cornbread gluten free, or gluten free croutons instead of wheat-based bread. It delivers the same classic stuffing flavor, savory aroma, and herby taste as traditional stuffing — without gluten.

Also known as:

  • Stuffing without gluten

  • Wheat free stuffing

  • Celiac friendly stuffing

When prepared correctly, it’s foolproof, easy, and every bit as delicious as traditional stuffing.

How to Make Gluten Free Stuffing from Scratch (Step-by-Step)

Step 1: Prepare the Bread

  • Cube gluten free bread

  • Dry bread overnight on a baking sheet
    This prevents mushy stuffing and ensures proper absorption.

Step 2: Sauté the Vegetables

  • Melt butter (or use olive oil)

  • Sauté onions and celery

  • Add garlic and cook until fragrant

This builds the base flavor for herby stuffing.

Step 3: Add Herbs and Seasoning

  • Add herbs and seasoning

  • Use sage, thyme, rosemary, parsley, poultry seasoning, salt, and black pepper

Step 4: Combine Wet and Dry Ingredients

  • Add bread cubes

  • Slowly pour in broth

  • Combine wet and dry ingredients gently

Step 5: Bake or Cook

  • Bake stuffing in oven
    or

  • Use stovetop gluten free stuffing
    or

  • Make slow cooker stuffing

Step 6: Check Moisture & Rest

  • Check internal moisture

  • Rest before serving for best texture

Gluten Free Stuffing Variations

Gluten Free Stuffing with Bread

The most traditional option using gluten free bread cubes.

Gluten Free Stuffing Without Bread

Made with vegetables, rice, or cornbread alternatives.

Gluten Free Cornbread Stuffing

Use gluten free cornbread or cornbread gluten free for a slightly sweet flavor.

Gluten Free Stuffing with Sausage

Adds protein and bold savory flavor.

Gluten Free Vegetarian Stuffing

Uses vegetable broth and extra herbs.

Gluten Free Vegan Stuffing

Swap butter for olive oil, skip eggs, and use vegetable broth.

Moist vs Crispy Stuffing (How to Control Texture)

Moist Gluten Free Stuffing

  • More broth

  • Covered baking

Crispy Gluten Free Stuffing

  • Less liquid

  • Uncovered baking

Soft Stuffing

  • Balanced moisture

  • Gentle mixing

Make Ahead & Storage Tips

Make Ahead Stuffing

  • Assemble and refrigerate up to 24 hours

Freezer Friendly Stuffing

  • Freeze unbaked or baked stuffing

Reheating Tips

  • Cover with foil

  • Add splash of broth

Taste Comparison: Gluten-Free vs Traditional Stuffing

Does gluten free stuffing taste different?
Not when done right. With proper drying and seasoning, it delivers the same classic stuffing flavor, savory stuffing, and herby stuffing profile as wheat-based versions.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ Schema)

Is stuffing gluten free?

Traditional stuffing is not, but gluten free versions are safe when made with gluten free bread.

What bread is best for gluten free stuffing?

Udi’s gluten free bread and Canyon Bakehouse gluten free bread work best.

How do you keep gluten free stuffing from getting mushy?

Dry bread overnight and add broth slowly.

Can you make gluten free stuffing ahead of time?

Yes, it’s perfect for make ahead stuffing.

Can gluten free stuffing be frozen?

Yes, it’s freezer friendly stuffing.

Is gluten free stuffing safe for celiac disease?

Yes, when using certified gluten free ingredients.

Can I make gluten free stuffing vegan?

Absolutely — use olive oil and vegetable broth.

Can I cook gluten free stuffing in a crock pot?

Yes, crock pot gluten free stuffing works great.

How do you dry gluten free bread for stuffing?

Cube and leave uncovered overnight or bake briefly.

Does gluten free stuffing taste different?

Not when properly seasoned it tastes classic and savory.

Final Thoughts: The Ultimate Gluten Free Stuffing Recipe

This easy, best, ultimate, and foolproof gluten free stuffing recipe proves that gluten free doesn’t mean flavor-free. Whether you’re serving it for Thanksgiving, Christmas, or a cozy dinner, this homemade gluten free stuffing delivers comfort, tradition, and confidence no gluten required.
